paras: The killing of Jim Harrington was the shooting of a Black farm worker by four masked men near Farmerville, Louisiana, on the evening of Friday, March 30, 1888. The men took him from the field where he was plowing, led him into the Loutre swamp with a rope around his neck, and shot him; a coroner's investigation could not identify them. The local paper called it "a murder surrounded with mystery."

According to the Farmerville Gazette, four masked men armed with Winchester rifles and a shotgun were seen at about 4 o'clock that afternoon riding along the public road toward the field, about seven miles north-east of Farmerville, where Harrington was plowing. After finding him, they led him into the Loutre swamp with a plow line fastened around his neck. The Gazette supposed that he broke loose and was about to escape when both barrels of a shotgun were fired at him, the buckshot striking him in the back near the shoulders and in the side of the head.

The coroner's investigation "failed to bring to light the perpetrators," though it established the account of the masked riders. No report of an arrest or of any accusation against Harrington appears in the coverage, and no motive was given.

The killing is known from a single item, first printed in the Farmerville Gazette of April 4 and reprinted on April 14 in the St. Landry Democrat's "Louisiana News" column, among notices of fires, land sales and elections. The item framed the killing as a mystery and a "murder," did not use the word lynching, and offered no explanation for why the men sought Harrington out. No other contemporary report of the killing appears in the coverage.

Four masked men seized Harrington, led him off with a rope round his neck and shot him, an illegal killing by a group of three or more (A1); the report names no accusation or motive, so the pretext of justice, race or tradition is not shown.

Consistent: 'last Friday evening' in the Gazette of Wednesday, April 4, 1888 is March 30 by inference.

Probable lynching: four masked men, rope round the neck, killing; no accusation or motive reported.
